sections.heading: String Replacement – Prefer replace() Over replaceAll()

items: Use replace() instead of replaceAll() when not using regex patterns.
replaceAll() expects the first parameter to be a regular expression. Using plain strings causes unnecessary performance cost.
Avoid recompiling the same regex repeatedly.
Store compiled patterns in static final fields for reuse.
Methods like String.matches() and String.split() internally compile regex patterns, causing performance issues.
Use java.io.File instead of raw String paths for portability.
Prefer FileReader/FileWriter with proper encoding (e.g., UTF-8).
Always close files using try-with-resources.
Avoid relying on platform default encoding.
Faster due to pre-compilation.
Prevents SQL injection.

content.text: ✔ Close All Resources in finally or Use Try-with-Resources:

items: Always close Connection, Statement, ResultSet.
Align method with column type (e.g., getString() for VARCHAR).
Promotes database portability and reduces migration effort.
Prefer Type 4 (native) drivers for better performance.
Efficient and scalable thread management.
Prevents data inconsistency and concurrency issues.
Avoid locking unnecessary code blocks to boost performance.
Reduces shared-state issues.
Can cause data races unless used as static final.
Prefer ConcurrentHashMap over synchronized collections.

content.text: InputThread: Randomly modifies (adds/removes) entries in the map.
OutputThread: Continuously reads map entries and prints them.
This program runs forever because the threads run an infinite loop, so you need to terminate the program and observe the output.

items: The Output thread lets you know that the map is constantly updated by the Input threads.

No synchronized block needed due to thread-safe map.
